Definition: from G4862 and G3880; to take along in company:--take with.
BiblicalUsage: Barnabas determines to take John Mark with them, and years later Paul goes up to Jerusalem with Barnabas and takes Titus with him also. Taking someone along is how the gospel travels: nobody goes alone, and the ones taken along become the next ones sent.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the gospel moves on companionship, and I believe taking someone with me is one of the best ways to serve Christ.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
